date_note: SRF's report of 20 November gives the canton's disclosure; it does not say when the attack happened or was found.
title: Canton Basel-Landschaft says data on about 97,000 cross-border commuters was taken in cyberattack
summary: Canton Basel-Landschaft told SRF a massive, broad cyberattack on its administration was stopped quickly, but forensic analysis showed one file was taken. SRF reports it holds about 97,000 records of cross-border commuters, with name, address, date of birth, civil status, job function, a Zemis number and employer contacts. The canton filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons.
plain: Swiss canton Basel-Landschaft says a file with data on about 97,000 cross-border commuters was stolen. It warns those affected to watch for phishing.
exec: A cantonal administration lost a file on about 97,000 people; affected people face phishing and identity-theft risk, per the canton.
action: Affected cross-border commuters: be careful with phishing attempts, as the canton warns.

validation.note: SRF read, relaying the canton's government spokesperson. Badische Zeitung report on the same story answered 403 and could not be read.
